mainTopic: The בן פקועה (live fetus in a slaughtered animal): the limits of its leniency, its blood, using it to redeem a firstborn donkey, and whether it is one body with its mother for טומאה.
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה. רבי שמעון שזורי says that a live fetus is permitted by its mother's שחיטה even after it grows up, but if the mother was torn instead of slaughtered, the fetus needs its own שחיטה. In the גמרא, רבי אושעיא limits the חכמים' leniency. A first version says it excludes the fetus's חלב and גיד הנשה, but both are disputed between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. So the teaching is restated: the leniency covers only eating, and it leaves out רביעה and plowing with another species. ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן then argue whether the fetus's blood follows its fat. Through רבי זירא and רב יוסף, this becomes a question of whether the blood carries כרת. Next the גמרא asks whether a בן פקועה can be used to redeem a firstborn donkey. מר זוטרא says no and רב אשי says yes, and they debate the גזירה שוה of "שה" from the פסח. Finally, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether the fetus is a separate body or one body with its mother for טומאה, and each challenges the other from sources about what makes the fetus ready to receive טומאה.

steps.title: Even a grown animal is permitted by its mother's slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי rules that an animal found alive inside its slaughtered mother never needs its own שחיטה, even years later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי says: even if the calf grew up, is five years old and plows in the field, the שחיטה of its mother still permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the most extreme version of the lenient view. A fetus permitted by its mother's שחיטה stays permitted forever, even as a grown working animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים in the משנה said a live nine-month fetus is permitted by its mother's שחיטה. רבי שמעון שזורי pushes this all the way: growing up and living a normal life does not change its status. In his view the mother's שחיטה counts as this animal's שחיטה for good.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'purifies it'; here it means 'makes it permitted to eat'
Plowing in the field, meaning a fully grown working animal

steps.confusionAlert: מטהרתו here does not mean טומאה and טהרה in the usual sense. It means the mother's שחיטה makes the offspring permitted to eat without its own שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
Even if it is five years old
and plowing in the field,
the slaughter of its mother makes it permitted.
phrases.notes: Literally 'purifies it', but here it just means he may eat it without slaughtering it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's dispute about a live nine-month fetus found in a slaughtered animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mother's שחיטה permits the offspring permanently, even after it is born and grows up.

steps.title: If the mother was torn, not slaughtered, the fetus needs its own slaughter
steps.stepSummary: If the mother was killed without שחיטה, a live nine-month fetus inside needs its own שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone tore the mother open and found a live nine-month fetus inside, it needs שחיטה, because its mother was not slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where even the lenient view agrees the fetus needs its own שחיטה. That is because the mother never had a kosher שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency depends entirely on the mother's שחיטה. Here there was no שחיטה of the mother, so there is nothing to carry over to the fetus. The fetus is then treated like any live animal.

keyTerms.meaning: He tore it open; he killed it without a proper שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: The fetus is permitted only through its mother's שחיטה. No שחיטה of the mother means no permission for the fetus.

phrases.english: If he tore it open and found in it
phrases.notes: He killed the mother by tearing, not by a kosher שחיטה.

phrases.english: a live nine-month fetus,
it requires slaughter,
because its mother was not slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְרָעָהּ וּמָצָא בָּהּ בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה חַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limit of the leniency in step 1: it works only when the mother was actually slaughtered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A live fetus found in a torn (unslaughtered) mother requires its own שחיטה.

steps.title: The leniency applies only to the matter of slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא limits the חכמים' leniency for the live fetus to the question of שחיטה alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: the חכמים treated it as permitted only regarding שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a statement that narrows the חכמים' view. The fetus is exempt from שחיטה, but that does not mean it is treated as part of the mother in every way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think that if the mother's שחיטה permits the fetus, the fetus is simply like a limb of the mother. רבי אושעיא says no: the exemption covers only שחיטה. In other matters it may still be treated as its own animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
They did not treat it leniently

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement drives the rest of the section. The גמרא will now ask what it is meant to exclude.

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
They did not treat it leniently
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים of the משנה, who said its mother's שחיטה permits it.

phrases.english: except regarding matters of slaughter alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by limiting the scope of the משנה's leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fetus is treated as part of its mother only for the purposes of שחיטה.

steps.title: What does this limitation exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference רבי אושעיא's limitation makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question. It sets up the next step, which will name what is excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'only' in רבי אושעיא's statement must be leaving something out. The גמרא wants to know which law, other than שחיטה, still treats the fetus as its own animal.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude what? Asked when a statement limits something

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical result of step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which laws are left out by saying the leniency applies only to שחיטה.

steps.title: It excludes the forbidden fat and the sciatic nerve
steps.stepSummary: The limitation means the fetus's חלב and גיד הנשה are still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It excludes its forbidden fat and its sciatic nerve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the fetus's חלב and גיד הנשה stay forbidden. In these matters it is treated as a separate animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fetus were fully part of the mother, maybe its fat and nerve would be permitted like other inner parts. רבי אושעיא is teaching that only the שחיטה is borrowed from the mother. The prohibitions of חלב and גיד הנשה still apply to it as its own animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: To exclude its forbidden fat and its sciatic nerve.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי חֶלְבּוֹ וְגִידוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limitation excludes the fetus's חלב and גיד הנשה, which remain forbidden.

steps.title: Which fat is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which fat רבי אושעיא was referring to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The fat of what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for more detail about the answer just given. This sets up two possible readings, which it will test one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Its fat' could mean the regular forbidden fat of the fetus. It could also mean the fat around the גיד הנשה. The גמרא will check whether each reading fits a statement that everyone accepts.

phrases.english: The fat of what?

steps.triggerLanguage: חֶלְבּוֹ דְּמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the answer in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'its fat' means the fetus's regular חלב or the fat of the גיד.

steps.title: The fetus's own fat cannot be meant, because it is disputed
steps.stepSummary: The fetus's regular fat is a matter of dispute, so רבי אושעיא could not have stated a simple rule about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the fat of the fetus, that is disputed! A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר says גיד הנשה applies to a fetus and its fat is forbidden; רבי יהודה says it does not apply and its fat is permitted. And רבי אושעיא himself said this dispute is about a live nine-month fetus, each following his view in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first reading and rejects it. The fetus's regular fat is a matter of argument, so רבי אושעיא could not state a flat rule that it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא himself explained that the ברייתא's argument is about a live nine-month fetus. רבי מאיר treats it as a full animal, so its fat is forbidden. רבי יהודה follows the חכמים of the משנה, who treat it as part of the mother, so he permits its fat. That means on the חכמים' view the fat is permitted, which contradicts reading רבי אושעיא as forbidding it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a reading that is about to be rejected
He follows his own known view

steps.confusionAlert: Note the pairing: in this ברייתא רבי יהודה takes the side of the חכמים of the משנה (the fetus is part of the mother). That is why his permitting the fat is a problem for reading רבי אושעיא's rule as following the חכמים.

phrases.english: If you say: the fat of the fetus,
they disagree about that!
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
The sciatic nerve prohibition applies to a fetus
and its fat is forbidden,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
it does not apply to a fetus
and its fat is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
the dispute is about a live nine-month fetus,
and Rabbi Meir follows his own view,
phrases.notes: In the משנה רבי מאיר said a live nine-month fetus needs its own שחיטה, so it is a full animal.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda follows his own view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא: חֶלְבּוֹ דִּשְׁלִיל, מִפְלָג פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible meaning of 'its fat' from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'its fat' in רבי אושעיא's statement as the fetus's regular חלב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אושעיא himself ties the ברייתא's argument to the משנה's argument. On the חכמים' (רבי יהודה's) side, the fetus's fat is permitted, so it cannot be something his statement says stays forbidden.

steps.title: The fat of the nerve cannot be meant either, because it is also disputed
steps.stepSummary: The second reading, the fat around the גיד הנשה, is also a subject of argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the fat of the nerve? That is also disputed, as a ברייתא teaches: with the גיד הנשה, one digs after it wherever it is and cuts out its fat from the root, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: one trims it level with the surface.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second meaning: the fat attached to the גיד. It rejects that as well, since רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about how much of this fat must be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר requires digging out the nerve everywhere and removing all its fat. רבי יהודה only requires trimming it even with the surface of the meat. Since this fat is also disputed, it does not work as the simple thing רבי אושעיא's statement excludes. The next step solves this by restating רבי אושעיא's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new attempt after the first one failed
Its fat (the fat around the nerve)
The smooth surface of the meat

steps.whatToRemember: Both readings of 'its fat' run into a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. The next step solves this by restating רבי אושעיא's teaching.

phrases.english: Rather, the fat of the nerve:
they disagree about that too,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
The sciatic nerve: one digs after it
wherever it is,
and cuts out its fat from the root,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
one trims it level with the surface.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, חֶלְבּוֹ דְּגִיד מִפְלָג פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of 'its fat' after step 7 rejected the first, and rejects that too.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'its fat' in רבי אושעיא's statement as the fat of the גיד הנשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fat of the גיד is itself the subject of a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, so it does not fit as a simple, agreed-upon exclusion.

steps.title: Rabbi Oshaya's teaching restated: only about eating
steps.stepSummary: Because both readings about fat were disputed, the גמרא restates רבי אושעיא's teaching. The leniency for the fetus applies only to eating, which leaves out רביעה and plowing with another species.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, it was said like this: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: The fetus was treated leniently only for eating. This leaves out mating with it and plowing with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier version of רבי אושעיא's teaching and gives a corrected version that avoids the challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier version said the limitation meant the fetus's חלב is still forbidden, but that is a disputed matter. The new version says the limitation is about non-eating laws. The fetus counts as a full animal for the laws of רביעה and כלאים, and everyone agrees about that.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, it was said like this. This introduces a corrected version of a teaching.
One who mates with the animal (רביעה)
One who plows with it together with a different species (כלאים)

steps.whatToRemember: In the final version, רבי אושעיא's limitation is about non-eating laws (רביעה and plowing), not about חלב or גיד הנשה.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
They did not treat it leniently except
phrases.notes: Literally "they did not go with it." He means the חכמים only ruled the fetus permitted without its own שחיטה in this area.

phrases.english: with regard to matters of eating alone,
to exclude one who mates with it, and one who plows with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אִתְּמַר – הָכִי אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problems raised in steps 7 and 8 by replacing the earlier version of רבי אושעיא's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the teaching (אי אתמר הכי אתמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The limitation meant the fetus's חלב and גיד הנשה stay forbidden, but those are disputed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limitation leaves out רביעה and plowing, which apply to the fetus according to everyone.

steps.title: Dispute: does the fetus's blood follow its fat?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the blood follows the fat: whoever permits the fat permits the blood, and whoever forbids the fat forbids the blood. רבי יוחנן says that even the one who permits the fat forbids the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: According to the one who permits its fat, he permits its blood. According to the one who forbids its fat, he forbids its blood. רבי יוחנן said: Even the one who permits its fat forbids its blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a dispute between אמוראים about the blood of the fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we saw that רבי יהודה permits the fetus's fat and רבי מאיר forbids it. ריש לקיש links the blood to the fat, so the two rulings go together. רבי יוחנן separates them: the blood is forbidden even according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who permits its fat (רבי יהודה)
The one who forbids its fat (רבי מאיר)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
According to the one who permits its fat, he permits its blood;
phrases.notes: This means רבי יהודה, from the argument mentioned before.

phrases.english: according to the one who forbids its fat, he forbids its blood.
phrases.notes: This means רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף לְדִבְרֵי הַמַּתִּיר בְּחֶלְבּוֹ – אוֹסֵר בְּדָמוֹ.
phrases.english: Even according to the one who permits its fat, he forbids its blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: לְדִבְרֵי הַמַּתִּיר בְּחֶלְבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about the fetus's fat and applies it to blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: blood follows fat. רבי יוחנן: blood is forbidden even according to the one who permits fat.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from the משנה: tear it and remove its blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן cites the משנה, which says to tear the fetus and remove its blood. This shows the blood is forbidden even though the rest of the fetus, including its fat, is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: The משנה says, 'He tears it open and removes its blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view using a line from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires removing the blood but does not require removing the fat. So the fat is permitted and the blood is still forbidden. That contradicts ריש לקיש's rule that whoever permits the fat permits the blood.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
"He tears it open and removes its blood."
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה about a fetus found in a slaughtered animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that whoever permits the fat permits the blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids the blood while treating the rest of the fetus, including the fat, as permitted. So the blood does not follow the fat.

steps.title: רבי זירא: ריש לקיש only meant there is no כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that ריש לקיש never said the blood is fully permitted. He only meant that eating it does not carry the punishment of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: He meant to say that one is not punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends ריש לקיש by narrowing what ריש לקיש meant by 'permits its blood.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Permits' here does not mean you may eat it. It means the blood does not carry the severe punishment of כרת, though it is still forbidden. So the משנה's demand to remove the blood fits ריש לקיש after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating real blood

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read ריש לקיש as saying the blood may be eaten. After רבי זירא, the argument is only about whether there is כרת. Both agree the blood is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
He meant to say that one is not punished with כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש meant the blood is fully permitted, which clashes with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש only meant there is no כרת. The blood is still forbidden, so it must be removed.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה gives כרת even for דם התמצית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view ריש לקיש was explaining. It would be רבי יהודה, who permits the fat. But at worst this blood is like דם התמצית, and רבי יהודה holds that even דם התמצית carries כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom did he say this? According to רבי יהודה? This blood should be no worse than דם התמצית, as it was taught: דם התמצית carries a regular prohibition. רבי יהודה says it carries כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's explanation of ריש לקיש by citing a ברייתא that shows רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's 'no כרת' must follow רבי יהודה, the one who permits the fat. The fetus's blood did not come out during the שחיטה, but at the very least it should count as דם התמצית, the blood that oozes out after the main spurt. The ברייתא says רבי יהודה gives כרת even for דם התמצית, so how could ריש לקיש say there is no כרת according to him?

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom are they saying this?
Let it be no worse than; at the least it is like
Blood that oozes out after the main spurt of שחיטה

phrases.english: According to whom are they saying this? According to Rabbi Yehuda?
Let it be no worse than blood of exudate,
as it is taught: Blood of exudate carries a regular prohibition;
Rabbi Yehuda says: It carries כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן קָאָמְרִי? לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא דַּם הַתַּמְצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's explanation from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's explanation that ריש לקיש means there is no כרת according to the one who permits the fat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The one who permits the fat is רבי יהודה, and he gives כרת even for דם התמצית. The fetus's blood is at least like דם התמצית, so according to him it should carry כרת.

steps.title: Lifeblood and draining blood go together for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that for רבי יהודה, the extra word "כל" in "כל דם" links דם התמצית to דם הנפש. If דם הנפש carries no כרת, as with a fetus, then דם התמצית carries no כרת either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף, the son of רב סלא the pious, explained before רב פפא: רבי יהודה learns from "blood" and "any blood." Wherever someone is liable for the lifeblood, he is also liable for the draining blood. Wherever someone is not liable for the lifeblood, he is not liable for the draining blood either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 13. It shows how רבי יהודה can hold that a fetus's blood does not carry כרת, even though he normally gives כרת for דם התמצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that רבי יהודה always gives כרת for דם התמצית. The answer is that, for him, דם התמצית only carries כרת when the same animal's דם הנפש carries כרת. A fetus is not treated as a separate life with its own דם הנפש, so neither kind of its blood carries כרת, though it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifeblood: the blood that spurts out at the moment of slaughter
Draining blood: the blood that oozes out after the main spurt
"Any blood": the wording of the פסוק that רבי יהודה reads as teaching a link between the two kinds of blood

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, דם התמצית follows דם הנפש. A fetus has no כרת-level lifeblood, so its draining blood carries no כרת either. This fits רבי זירא's reading of ריש לקיש.

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְגְּמָא רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא
phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rav Salla the Pious, explained it
before Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה ״דָּם״ וְ״כׇל דָּם״,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds of "blood" and "any blood"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:10. The פסוק could have just said "blood," so the extra word "any" teaches something.

phrases.english: wherever one is liable for the lifeblood,
one is liable for the draining blood;

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּלָא מִחַיַּיב אַדַּם הַנֶּפֶשׁ –
phrases.english: and wherever one is not liable for the lifeblood,
one is not liable for the draining blood.
phrases.notes: "Liable" here means liable for כרת, as in the last few steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמָא רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13, which asked how רבי יהודה could free fetal blood from כרת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of a פסוק that limits the rule being challenged
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה gives כרת for דם התמצית in every case, so a fetus's blood should carry כרת too.
steps.terutzMaskana: "כל דם" links the two kinds of blood. Draining blood carries כרת only where lifeblood does, and a fetus's lifeblood does not.

steps.title: Can a בן פקועה be used to redeem a firstborn donkey?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a בן פקועה can serve as the lamb used to redeem a firstborn donkey. According to רבי מאיר there is no question, because he requires it to be slaughtered, so it is a full lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: may one redeem a firstborn donkey with a בן פקועה? According to רבי מאיר you would not need to ask. Since he says it needs its own slaughter, it is a full lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a בן פקועה. It first narrows the question by showing that according to רבי מאיר the answer is simple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says a firstborn donkey is redeemed with a שה (lamb). רבי מאיר holds that a בן פקועה needs שחיטה of its own, which means he treats it as a normal living animal. So it clearly counts as a שה.

keyTerms.meaning: A live calf or lamb found inside its mother after she was slaughtered
To redeem, here meaning to redeem a firstborn donkey with a lamb

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
What is the law about redeeming with a ben pekua?
phrases.notes: He means redeeming a firstborn donkey, which the תורה says to redeem with a lamb (שמות 13:13).

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir, you need not ask,
since he says it requires slaughter,
it is a full-fledged lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִפְדּוֹת בְּבֶן פְּקוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the בן פקועה after the discussion of blood ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a בן פקועה counts as a שה for redeeming a firstborn donkey.

steps.title: According to the רבנן: plain meat or a living lamb?
steps.stepSummary: The question only applies according to the רבנן, who say the mother's slaughter makes the fetus permitted. Is it then like meat in a basket, or is it a lamb because it walks around alive?
steps.simpleTranslation: The question is according to the רבנן, who say that the mother's slaughter makes it permitted. What is the law? Since they say the mother's slaughter makes it permitted, maybe it is like meat in a basket. Or perhaps, since it runs back and forth, we call it a lamb?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the question and lays out the two sides according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, a בן פקועה was already made permitted by its mother's שחיטה, so in law it may look like meat that has already been slaughtered, and meat cannot be used to redeem a donkey. On the other hand, it is physically alive and walking, so maybe it still counts as a שה.

keyTerms.meaning: Its mother's slaughter makes it permitted
Like meat in a basket: already slaughtered meat, not a living animal
Runs back and forth, meaning it is clearly alive
We call it by that name

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the animal is physically alive. The question is whether, in הלכה, it counts as a living lamb or as meat that is already permitted.

phrases.english: When should you ask? According to the Rabbis,
who say: its mother's slaughter makes it permitted. What is the law?
Since they say its mother's slaughter makes it permitted,
it is like meat in a basket,
phrases.notes: In other words, it is just a piece of meat, and you can't redeem a donkey with meat.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּרָהֵיט וְאָזֵיל וְרָהֵיט וְאָתֵי –
phrases.english: or perhaps, since it runs off and runs back,
we call it a "lamb"?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question from Step 15 to the view of the רבנן and lays out both sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן's view that the mother's שחיטה permits the fetus makes it count as meat, or whether its being alive makes it count as a שה.

steps.title: מר זוטרא and רב אשי disagree
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא rules that one may not redeem a donkey with a בן פקועה. רב אשי rules that one may.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: one may not redeem with it. רב אשי said: one may redeem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא holds that a בן פקועה does not count as a proper שה for this מצוה. רב אשי holds that it does, so it can be used. The next steps test what מר זוטרא's source is.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not redeem with it

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, whether a בן פקועה counts as a שה for redeeming a firstborn donkey is a dispute. מר זוטרא says no, and רב אשי says yes.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: One may not redeem,
and Rav Ashi said: One may redeem.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא אָמַר: אֵין פּוֹדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two opposing answers to the question raised in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מר זוטרא says a בן פקועה cannot be used to redeem a donkey, and רב אשי says it can.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question is left as a dispute between מר זוטרא and רב אשי.

steps.title: רב אשי asks מר זוטרא for his reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks מר זוטרא whether his ruling comes from a link between the word "שה" by a firstborn donkey and "שה" by the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to מר זוטרא: What is your reasoning? Is it that you learn "lamb" from "lamb" written by the פסח offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks מר זוטרא to explain why he said a בן פקועה cannot redeem a donkey. He suggests a reason so that he can test it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי guesses that מר זוטרא uses a גזירה שוה. The word "שה" appears both by פדיון פטר חמור and by the קרבן פסח, so the rules of the פסח lamb would carry over. A בן פקועה would not be a proper lamb for a פסח, so it would not work for the donkey either.

keyTerms.meaning: To learn one law from another source, here through a matching word
Lamb or sheep. The word appears both by the firstborn donkey and by the פסח

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Mar Zutra:
What is your reasoning?
Is it that you learn "lamb" "lamb" from the Pesach offerings?
phrases.notes: The word "שה" appears by the donkey in שמות 13:13 and by the פסח in שמות 12:5.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דַּעְתָּךְ? דְּגָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Probes the source behind מר זוטרא's ruling from Step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מר זוטרא's ruling rests on a גזירה שוה of "שה" "שה" from the קרבן פסח

steps.title: Then the lamb should also need to be male, unblemished and one year old
steps.stepSummary: If the rules of the פסח lamb carry over, then the redemption lamb should also have to be male, תמים, and within its first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there it must be male, unblemished and in its first year, so too here it should have to be male, unblemished and in its first year!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the reason he just suggested. If you copy the פסח rules, you must copy all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח lamb must be male, without a blemish, and in its first year. If the גזירה שוה brings those rules over, the redemption lamb would need all three as well. That is not the הלכה, so the link seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as there, so too here. This is how the comparison of a גזירה שוה works

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן – זָכָר, תָּמִים, וּבֶן שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: If so, just as there it must be male, unblemished, and in its first year,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן – זָכָר, תָּמִים, וּבֶן שָׁנָה!
phrases.english: so too here it should be male, unblemished, and in its first year!
phrases.notes: The point is that this is not the הלכה. A redemption lamb can be female, blemished, or older.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the גזירה שוה suggested in Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה "שה" "שה" from the קרבן פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would bring in every פסח requirement, and that is not the halacha for redeeming a donkey

steps.title: The doubled word "redeem" widens the rule
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that the doubled word "תפדה" includes lambs that are not male, not unblemished, or not in their first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You shall redeem," "you shall redeem" comes to include more.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא defends his reasoning. A separate word in the פסוק cancels the male, unblemished and one-year requirements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "תפדה" twice. That extra wording is a ריבוי, an inclusion. It brings in lambs that the פסח comparison would have left out. The גזירה שוה can stay, but those three rules do not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: It included more, widening the rule

phrases.english: "You shall redeem," "you shall redeem" included more.
phrases.notes: שמות 13:13: "תפדה בשה, ואם לא תפדה".

steps.triggerLanguage: ״תִּפְדֶּה״ ״תִּפְדֶּה״ רִיבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate ריבוי in the פסוק overrides parts of the גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All the פסח requirements carry over to the redemption lamb
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the doubled "תפדה", male, unblemished and first-year are not required

steps.title: Then include every kind of lamb
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks: if "תפדה" "תפדה" widens the rule, why not include every lamb, even a בן פקועה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If "you shall redeem," "you shall redeem" includes more, then let it include everything too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי turns מר זוטרא's answer back against him. If the inclusion works, it should also include a בן פקועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ריבוי can undo the פסח requirements, it should be able to undo all of them. Then there is no reason to leave out a בן פקועה, which matches רב אשי's own ruling.

phrases.english: If "you shall redeem," "you shall redeem" includes more,
then let it include even everything too,
phrases.notes: He means: a בן פקועה should be included as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״תִּפְדֶּה״ ״תִּפְדֶּה״ רִיבָּה, אֲפִילּוּ כֹּל מִילֵּי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's use of the ריבוי of "תפדה"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inclusion that cancels some פסח requirements should cancel all of them, including the exclusion of a בן פקועה

steps.title: Otherwise the link of "lamb" would teach nothing
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that if "תפדה" included everything, the גזירה שוה of "שה" "שה" would have no purpose. So it must still exclude the בן פקועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does "lamb" "lamb" accomplish for you?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא defends himself one last time. The גזירה שוה must still teach something, and what it teaches is to leave out a בן פקועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources in the פסוק must have a job. The ריבוי includes female, blemished and older lambs. The גזירה שוה still excludes a בן פקועה. If the ריבוי included everything, the "שה" link would be wasted, and the תורה does not write words for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it accomplish for you? What is it for?

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא keeps both sources working. The doubled "תפדה" includes female, blemished and older lambs. The link of "שה" to the פסח still excludes a בן פקועה.

phrases.english: If so, what does "lamb" "lamb" accomplish for you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן ״שֶׂה״ ״שֶׂה״ מַאי אַהֲנִי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source must have a purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ריבוי includes every kind of lamb, even a בן פקועה
steps.terutzMaskana: The ריבוי includes a lot, but the גזירה שוה still excludes a בן פקועה

steps.title: Does the fetus count as a separate level of impurity?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: can a בן פקועה inside its slaughtered mother count as a separate level of טומאה, with the mother as ראשון and the fetus as שני?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: may one count in it first and second?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a בן פקועה, this time about טומאה. It asks whether the fetus counts as a level of impurity separate from its mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mother touches a source of טומאה, she becomes a ראשון לטומאה. If the fetus is its own separate item, it would only be a שני, one step further away. If it counts as part of the mother, it would be a ראשון just like her.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about the donkey any more. It is a brand-new question about levels of טומאה.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
What is the law about counting in it first and second?
phrases.notes: He means: is the mother a ראשון and the fetus inside her a שני?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִמְנוֹת בּוֹ רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a בן פקועה, following the רבנן's view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a בן פקועה inside its slaughtered mother is a separate item for counting levels of טומאה

steps.title: The fetus counts as a separate level of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the mother and the בן פקועה are counted as two levels: the mother is ראשון, the fetus is שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We count them as first and second.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer to the question from step 23. He says yes, the fetus is its own level of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טומאה touches the slaughtered mother, she becomes a ראשון לטומאה. The fetus inside her gets its טומאה from her, so it is one step weaker, a שני. This means רבי יוחנן treats the fetus as a separate body from its mother.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
We count with it a first and a second.
phrases.notes: He means the mother is the 'first' and the fetus inside her is the 'second'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מוֹנִין בּוֹ רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The mother is ראשון and the fetus is שני.

steps.title: The fetus is like a nut inside its shell
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש disagrees. The fetus is not a separate level; mother and fetus act as one unit, like a loose nut inside its shell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: We do not count them as first and second. It is like a nut that rattles inside its shell.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the opposite answer. The mother and fetus share the same level of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nut that rattles inside its shell is still treated as one item with the shell. In the same way, the fetus is treated as part of its mother. So if the mother is ראשון, the fetus is ראשון too.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't misread the nut picture. ריש לקיש is not saying the fetus is cut off from its mother. Even though it moves loosely like the nut, it still counts as one unit with her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
We do not count with it a first and a second;
it is like a nut
that rattles in its shell.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר: אֵין מוֹנִין בּוֹ רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing answer to רבי יוחנן's view in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Mother and fetus are one unit with the same level of טומאה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש quotes the משנה about the fetus's foreleg
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן. He begins by quoting the משנה about a fetus that stuck its foreleg out: רבי מאיר and the חכמים say the meat is טמא from touching the cut-off leg.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן: 'The meat has touched a נבלה. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: it has touched a slaughtered טרפה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. Here ריש לקיש only quotes the source. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, a fetus stuck its foreleg out of the mother before she was slaughtered. Then the leg was cut off. Either way (נבלה for רבי מאיר, טרפה שחוטה for the חכמים), the leg gives some טומאה to the meat it touches. Everyone agrees the meat can become טמא, and that fact is what ריש לקיש will use.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching a נבלה (an animal that died without proper שחיטה)
A slaughtered טרפה. By Torah law it is not טמא, but the רבנן gave it a light טומאה
The meat (here, the flesh that touched the cut-off leg)

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish challenged Rabbi Yochanan:
The meat is [טמא as] having touched a נבלה —
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה earlier (72a) about a fetus that stuck its foreleg out before its mother was slaughtered.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
[It has] touched a slaughtered טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens ריש לקיש's attack on רבי יוחנן's view from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the fetus is a separate body (step 24).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up the source. Both opinions in the משנה agree the meat can become טמא from the leg.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה on 72a about the fetus's foreleg.

steps.title: How did the fetus become ready to get טומאה?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains the attack. In his view the fetus is one body with its mother, so her slaughter blood made it ready to become טמא. In רבי יוחנן's view the fetus is separate, so what made it ready?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for me, since I say they are one body. That is how the fetus became ready for טומאה through its mother's blood. But for you, how did it become ready?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש now states the actual challenge. He shows that his own view explains the משנה and that רבי יוחנן's view seems to leave a gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it has been made wet by a proper liquid (הכשר). The mother's blood from her slaughter counts as that liquid. If the fetus is part of the mother, it was made ready along with her. If the fetus is a separate body, as רבי יוחנן says, nothing seems to have made it ready, so how could the משנה call its meat טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one side, but...)
Was made ready to receive טומאה (by getting wet)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's challenge rests on הכשר. Calling the fetus 'one body' with its mother explains how the mother's slaughter blood made it ready to become טמא. רבי יוחנן now has to explain how a separate fetus got this readiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links two areas of law. Whether the fetus is 'one body' with its mother affects both how we count levels of טומאה and how it becomes ready to receive טומאה at all.

phrases.english: It works well according to me,
since I say it is one body —
that is how it was made ready [for טומאה] through its mother's blood,
phrases.notes: Food can only become טמא after it gets wet. The blood from the mother's שחיטה counts as that wetting.

phrases.english: but according to you,
through what was it made ready?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְדִידִי, דְּאָמֵינָא חַד גּוּפָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the attack that uses the משנה quoted in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the fetus is a separate body.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה assumes the fetus's meat can become טמא, which requires הכשר. Only treating the fetus as one body with its mother explains where that הכשר came from: her slaughter blood.

steps.title: The slaughter itself made the fetus ready, following רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the fetus became ready for טומאה through the שחיטה of its mother, following the view of רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It became ready through the slaughter, and this follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's challenge from the last step. He explains what made the fetus ready to become טמא, even though he holds it is a separate body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש had asked: if the fetus is separate from its mother, her blood did not touch it, so what made it ready? רבי יוחנן answers that no liquid is needed. Following רבי שמעון, the שחיטה, which makes the meat permitted to eat, also makes it ready for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Being made ready (able) to receive טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Usually food becomes ready for טומאה only by touching a liquid. Here רבי יוחנן relies on רבי שמעון, who says the שחיטה alone can do the job, so the mother's blood is not needed.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is answering ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Through the slaughter,
phrases.notes: He means the שחיטה of the mother, which also permits the fetus.

phrases.english: and in accordance with רבי שמעון.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון holds that the meat of a slaughtered animal is ready for טומאה even without touching a liquid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּשְׁחִיטָה, וּכְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge from step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rely on a תנא (רבי שמעון) whose view removes the need for liquid
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that a separate fetus could only become ready by touching its mother's blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי שמעון, the שחיטה itself makes it ready, so it does not need to be one body with the mother.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן quotes a ברייתא about a בן פקועה crossing a river
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן now challenges ריש לקיש. He quotes a ברייתא: a בן פקועה that crossed a river became ready for טומאה, so if it then went to a cemetery, it is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן raised an objection to ריש לקיש: If it passed through a river, it became ready. If it then went to a cemetery, it became טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the sides switch, and רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the בן פקועה needed the river water to become ready for טומאה. This detail will be used against ריש לקיש in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Cemetery, a place that makes things טמא

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן raised an objection
to רבי שמעון בן לקיש:
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש, written with his full name.

phrases.english: If it passed through a river, it became ready,
phrases.notes: The subject is a בן פקועה that grew up. The river water made it ready for טומאה.

phrases.english: if it went to a cemetery, it became טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending himself, רבי יוחנן turns to attack ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that mother and fetus are one body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the ברייתא requires river water to make the בן פקועה ready; the attack is spelled out in the next step.

steps.title: Why would it need the river if its mother's blood already made it ready?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains his attack. In his view the fetus is a separate body, so it needs the river to become ready. In ריש לקיש's view it is one body with the mother, so her blood already made it ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for me, because I say they are two bodies. That is why only if it was made ready does it become טמא, and if not, it does not. But you say they are one body, so it was already made ready by its mother's blood!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן spells out why the ברייתא is a problem for ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fetus is separate (רבי יוחנן), it was never made ready by its mother's blood, so it makes sense that it needs the river. If it is one body with its mother (ריש לקיש), her slaughter blood already made it ready. Then the ברייתא should not need the river at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one view), introducing a contrast with another view

steps.whatToRemember: Each side uses the question of what made the fetus ready for טומאה. ריש לקיש asked how a separate fetus becomes ready. רבי יוחנן answered with רבי שמעון's view of שחיטה. Now רבי יוחנן asks why a fetus that is one body with its mother would ever need river water.

phrases.english: It works well according to me,
since I say they are two bodies,
because of that:
if it was made ready, yes (it becomes טמא),
if it was not made ready, no.
But according to you,
since you said it is one body,
it was already made ready through its mother's blood!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְדִידִי דְּאָמֵינָא תְּרֵי גּוּפֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the attack set up by the ברייתא in step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that mother and fetus are one body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they are one body, the mother's slaughter blood already made the fetus ready, so the ברייתא's requirement of river water makes no sense.
